p: a: The first part of the epistle contains a most profitable preface down to verse six.

Paul, exhorting the Romans to give diligent heed to him, in that he shows that he comes not in his own name, but as God's messenger to the Gentiles, entreats them with the weightiest matter that exists, promised long ago by God, by many good witnesses, and now at length indeed performed.
servant of Jesus Christ: Minister, for this word "servant" is not taken in this place as set against the word "freeman", but rather refers to and declares his ministry and office.

apostle: Whereas he said before in a general term that he was a minister, now he comes to a more special name, and says that he is an apostle, and that he did not take this office upon himself by his own doing, but that he was called by God, and therefore in this letter of his to the Romans he is doing nothing but his duty.
separated unto the gospel of God: Appointed by God to preach the gospel.

Concerning his: By declaring the sum of the doctrine of the Gospel, he stirs up the Romans to consider well the matter about which he is entreating them: so then he shows that Christ (who is the very substance and sum of the gospel) is the only Son of God the Father, who with regard to his humanity is born of the seed of David, but with regard to his divine and spiritual nature, by which he sanctified himself, is begotten of the Father from everlasting, as also manifestly appears by his mighty resurrection.
Son Jesus Christ our Lord: This is a plain testimony of the person of Christ, that he is but one, and also a testimony of his two natures, and their properties.
made of the seed of David: Who received flesh from the virgin who was David's daughter.
according to the flesh: As he is man: for this word "flesh", by the figure of speech synecdoche, is taken for man.
declared to be the Son of: Shown and made manifest.
power: The divine and mighty power is set against the weakness of the flesh, for it overcame death.
By whom we have received: Of whom.
grace and apostleship: This marvellous, liberal, and gracious gift, which is given to me, the least of all the saints, to preach, etc.; see Eph 3:8.
obedience to the faith: That men through faith might obey God.
among all nations: For his name's sake.
called of Jesus Christ: Who through God's goodness belong to Christ.
Grace to you and peace from: God's free good will: by "peace" the Hebrews mean a prosperous success in all things.
First: He obtains their favourable patience, in that he points out what it is that they can be praised for, and his true apostolic good will toward them, confirmed by taking God himself as witness.
spoken of throughout the: Because your faith is such that it is spoken well of in all churches.
whole world: In all churches.
spirit in the: Very willingly and with all my heart.
gospel of his Son: In preaching his Son.
I may be comforted together with: Though Paul was ever so excellent, yet in teaching the church, he might be instructed by it.
Rome also: He means all those who dwell at Rome, though some of them were not Romans; see the end of the epistle.

for it is the: This is the second part of the epistle, until the beginning of chapter nine. Now the whole end and purpose of the discussion is this: that is to say, to show that there is but one way to attain unto salvation (which is displayed to us by God in the gospel, and that equally to every nation), and this way is Jesus Christ apprehended by faith.
power of God unto salvation to: God's mighty and effectual instrument to save men by.
Greek: When this word "Greek" is contrasted with the word "Jew", then it signifies a Gentile.

For therein is the righteousness of: The confirmation of the former proposition: we are taught in the gospel that we are instituted before God by faith, which increases daily, and therefore also saved.
faith to faith: From faith, which increases daily.
as it is written: The proof of the first as well as of the second proposition, out of Habakkuk, who attributes and gives to faith both justice and life before God.

For the wrath of God is: Another confirmation of the principal question: all men being considered in themselves, or without Christ, are guilty both of ungodliness and also unrighteousness, and therefore are subject on condemnation: therefore they need to seek righteousness in someone else.
all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men: Against all types of ungodliness.

truth in unrighteousness: By "truth" Paul means all the light that is left in man since his fall, not as though they being led by this were able to come into favour with God, but that their own reason might condemn them of wickedness both against God and man.

Because that which may be known: By their ungodliness he proves that although all men have a most clear and evident mirror in which to behold the everlasting and almighty nature of God, even in his creatures, yet they have fallen away from those principles to most foolish and stupid ideas of their own brains, in their worship of God and of what God requires of them.
them: In their hearts.
understood by the things that are: You do not see God, and yet you acknowledge him as God by his works; Cicero.
glorified him not as God: They did not honour him with that honour and service which was appropriate for his everlasting power and Godhead.
vain in their imaginations: As if he said, became so corrupt in themselves.
Professing themselves to be wise: Or, thought themselves.
uncorruptible God into an image made: For the true God they substituted another.
Wherefore: The unrighteousness of men he sets forth first in this, that following their lusts, even against nature, they defiled themselves one with another, by the just judgment of God.
God also: The contempt of religion is the source of all evil.
gave them up to uncleanness through: As a just judge.
recompence of their error which was: An appropriate reward and that which they deserved.
And even as they did not: He proves the unrighteousness of man by referring to many types of wickedness, from which (if not from all, yet at the least from many of them) no man is altogether free.

reprobate mind: To a corrupt and perverse mind, by which it comes to pass that the conscience, having been removed by them, and they having almost no more remorse for sin, run headlong into all types of evil.
covenantbreakers: Not caring if they keep their covenants and bargains.
judgment of God: By the "judgment of God" he means that which the philosophers called the "law of nature", and the lawyers themselves termed the "law of nations".
have pleasure in them that do: Are companions and partakers with them in their wickedness, and beside that, commend those who do wrong.
